seed_commits.message:
chore: initial project scaffold

FastAPI service, MongoDB in compose and the CI skeleton. No application
code yet.
seed_commits.author: Noor Haddad <noor.haddad@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(models): event schema with UTC-only timestamps

A naive timestamp is rejected rather than assumed to be UTC. The assumption
holds until one gateway is misconfigured, and then the events are filed under
times they did not happen at with nothing in the data to show it.
seed_commits.author: Noor Haddad <noor.haddad@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(mongo): events collection, indexes and the write path

Deduplication is the unique index on event_id, not a read-then-write check.
The check is a race: two workers replaying the same retried batch both see
'absent' and both insert. Inserts are unordered so one duplicate cannot drop
the rest of the batch.
seed_commits.author: Tomas Lindqvist <tomas.lindqvist@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(api): ingest and recent-window endpoints

Every query in queries.py is bounded by a time range, a limit or both. An
operational endpoint whose cost grows with the age of the service works in
week one and pages somebody in month four.
seed_commits.author: Tomas Lindqvist <tomas.lindqvist@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(perfmodel): nearest-rank percentiles and Apdex

Nearest-rank rather than interpolated, so a reported p99 is a latency some
request actually experienced. perfmodel imports no storage: every statistic
is a pure function of numbers and can be tested against a hand computation.
seed_commits.author: Grace Oyelaran <grace.oyelaran@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(warehouse): DuckDB rollups fed from the event stream

The watermark tracks received_at, not occurred_at. Events arrive late, and a
watermark that has advanced past a late event's event time will never select
it; the current window stays plausible while older buckets quietly stop being
correct. Buckets are rebuilt rather than incremented so a late arrival can
correct history.
seed_commits.author: Grace Oyelaran <grace.oyelaran@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(cli): indexes, load, rollup, status and report

Thin by design -- each subcommand calls one library function, because a
pipeline step that only exists as a CLI subcommand cannot be unit tested.
seed_commits.author: Noor Haddad <noor.haddad@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
test: cover the stores, the pipeline and the first statistics

Mongo tests each get their own database, dropped afterwards. A missing
MongoDB fails rather than skips: a skipped test is green, and a suite that
goes green when the database is unreachable cannot tell 'this works' from
'this never ran'.
seed_commits.author: Tomas Lindqvist <tomas.lindqvist@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
ci: run the suite and a pipeline smoke against MongoDB

ci/run_ci.sh mirrors the workflow so the same steps can be run locally.
seed_commits.author: Noor Haddad <noor.haddad@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(data): deterministic seed generator and committed exports

Three hours of traffic with a deploy regression at 12:30, one buffered
gateway delivering late, and a retried batch. Fixed RNG seed, so every
environment gets byte-identical files and the integration tests can assert
exact totals.
seed_commits.author: Grace Oyelaran <grace.oyelaran@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(perfmodel): Wilson intervals and a seeded bootstrap

Error rates live near zero, where the normal approximation gives negative
lower bounds and, at zero errors, an interval of zero width. The bootstrap's
seed is a required keyword argument: an interval that differs between two
runs over the same data cannot be put in a report.
seed_commits.author: Grace Oyelaran <grace.oyelaran@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(perfmodel): Mann-Whitney U for release comparison

Latency is heavily right-skewed, so a t-test compares means that are
dominated by the tail. The tie correction is not optional: latencies are
whole milliseconds, ties are everywhere, and without it every z is pulled
towards zero.
seed_commits.author: Priya Raman <priya.raman@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(perfmodel): EWMA and CUSUM change detection

EWMA's memory decays geometrically, so it catches a spike and misses a small
sustained shift -- against a one-sigma step its weighted mean converges to
one sigma against a 1.26-sigma band and never alarms at all. CUSUM
accumulates. EWMA for incidents, CUSUM for deploys.
seed_commits.author: Priya Raman <priya.raman@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(perfmodel): seasonality-adjusted baseline on median and MAD

Tuesday 14:00 and Sunday 03:00 are not the same service, so the baseline is
keyed by hour of week. The centre is a median and the dispersion a MAD
because the history always contains last month's incident, and a standard
deviation inflated by one incident is what stops the next one from scoring.
seed_commits.author: Grace Oyelaran <grace.oyelaran@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(analytics): the statistics endpoints

analytics.py is the seam between perfmodel and storage: it turns a question
into a window, a query and a statistic. Every function takes its window
explicitly and none of them call utcnow(), so a report means the same thing
tomorrow.
seed_commits.author: Priya Raman <priya.raman@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
perf: measure what the server had to do, not how long it took

bench_query reports totalDocsExamined for the recent-window query. A
wall-clock number on a laptop running three other containers tells you about
the laptop; documents examined is identical on every machine and the gap
between a healthy value and an unhealthy one is a factor of a hundred.
seed_commits.author: Tomas Lindqvist <tomas.lindqvist@example.com>
